title: Per-element shot types (behavior + strong visuals): Fire single / Ice pierce / Electricity chain
description: Make each element FEEL like a distinct shot (DD-004 element identities + game-design 'readable VFX'), driven by the spell definition files (.tres). Today firebolt/ice_shard/lightning all reference the same scenes/projectile.tscn and differ only by stats (TASK-014 gave color+small shape); in the single-target arena the differences are invisible and the shots feel the same. Deliverables: (1) DATA-DRIVEN SHOT TYPE in SpellData: add an enum ShotType { SINGLE, PIERCE, CHAIN } and @export var shot_type plus a chain/pierce radius if needed; set firebolt = SINGLE, ice_shard = PIERCE (keep applies_slow=true, bump max_targets so it can pierce e.g. 3), lightning = CHAIN (max_targets 3). This makes 'each element has a shot type in the definition files' literally true. (2) BEHAVIOR in scripts/combat/projectile.gd honoring shot_type: SINGLE = stop/queue_free on first hit (Fire, high damage); PIERCE = pass straight THROUGH enemies in its path, hitting up to max_targets distinct enemies and applying slow (Ice; reuse the existing _remaining_targets/_hit pierce logic); CHAIN = on hit, REDIRECT toward the nearest not-yet-hit enemy within a radius and continue (Electricity arc/bounce), up to max_targets, each enemy hit once, no infinite loop. Extract the chain target selection into a PURE helper (e.g. scripts/combat/projectile_chain.gd: next_target(from_pos, candidates:Array[Vector2/Node], already_hit, radius) -> index/null) for headless testing. Enemies are discoverable via the 'enemies'/Enemies group or a passed candidate list; keep it null/empty safe. (3) STRONG VISUAL differentiation: noticeably distinct size per element (Fire bigger/heavier, Ice large angular shard, Electricity slim fast bolt) by scaling ProjectileStyle polygons or per-element scale, PLUS a cheap per-element TRAIL (a fading Line2D that records recent positions, tinted by the element color language, or a small trailing CPUParticles2D). Keep ProjectileStyle the single source of truth for color/shape; trails reuse the same color. Optionally a slightly stronger impact for Fire. Placeholder primitives only, no external art. (4) Keep collision layers (PlayerMagic 4 -> Enemies 3), rotation-aims-silhouette, matchup, and TASK-014 muzzle flash intact. Tests-first (GUT pure logic): shot_type drives behavior (SINGLE stops after 1, PIERCE continues up to max_targets through distinct enemies, CHAIN selects nearest-unhit-in-radius then stops when none/limit), the pure chain next_target helper (nearest first, excludes already-hit, bounded by radius + max_targets, empty/null safe, no repeats), and that ice_shard applies slow while piercing. Reuse existing combat test patterns/fakes. Follow Bash gotcha (never 'cd &&'; absolute --path; --import for new class_names). Verify headless clean + GUT exit 0, no regression. NOTE: the CHAIN mechanic is the foundation TASK-019 (Linked Swarm) will showcase.
acceptance_criteria: SpellData has a data-driven ShotType { SINGLE, PIERCE, CHAIN } enum + @export field; firebolt=SINGLE, ice_shard=PIERCE (applies_slow, max_targets>1), lightning=CHAIN (max_targets 3) are set in the .tres files.

Projectile honors shot_type: SINGLE stops on first hit (Fire, high damage); PIERCE passes through and hits up to max_targets distinct enemies applying slow (Ice); CHAIN redirects to the nearest not-yet-hit enemy within a radius and continues up to max_targets, each enemy hit once with no infinite loop (Electricity).
A pure, unit-tested chain target selector (nearest-unhit-within-radius, bounded by radius + max_targets, no repeats, empty/null safe) exists and drives the CHAIN behavior.

Shots are strongly visually distinct: noticeably different size per element + a cheap per-element trail tinted by the element color language (ProjectileStyle remains the single source of truth for color/shape); placeholder primitives only.

Collision layers, rotation-aimed silhouette, DD-006 matchup, and the TASK-014 muzzle flash are intact; GUT covers shot_type behavior (SINGLE/PIERCE/CHAIN), the chain selector, and ice pierce+slow; full suite passes headless exit 0 with no regression; project loads clean.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: Built tests-first; reviewer (fresh) APPROVE, no HIGH/MEDIUM. SpellData now has a data-driven ShotType {SINGLE,PIERCE,CHAIN} + chain_radius; firebolt=SINGLE (heavy 1-target), ice_shard=PIERCE (passes through up to max_targets=3, applies slow each), lightning=CHAIN (redirects to nearest unhit enemy in radius, max_targets=3) — chain via pure ProjectileChain.nearest_index, dedup by _hit, bounded by _remaining_targets + LIFETIME (no infinite loop / no re-hit). Per-element Sprite scale + fading Line2D trail tinted from ProjectileStyle (still single source of truth for color/shape; collision r=6 + rotation aim + matchup + muzzle flash intact). empire_drone.tscn joined the 'enemies' group for chain discovery (side-effect-free). ALSO fixed a TASK-015-introduced regression: test_magic_manager.gd was silently skipped by GUT (passed `self` (a Node) where cast_primary types origin Node2D -> parse error -> whole file ignored), so all 18 MagicManager tests incl. cast_failed/can_afford were not running; fixed by using a real Node2D origin. Suite 225->244 passing, exit 0, no parse errors / no ignored scripts, clean headless load. LOW/NIT only (pre-existing test_reticle FakeMagicManager typed-onready noise flagged for a cleanup ticket). Not committed (no git repo).
